subject: Release train coordination: quant profile route-config migration + canary plan (Mar 11–Mar 20)
body:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Mar 6, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Release train coordination: quant profile route-config migration + canary plan (Mar 11–Mar 20)

Sharing the proposed sequencing for the route-config migration + canary rollout for Quantization Profile Library (route-level opt-in).

Attachments:
- quant-profile-release-checklist-v0.3.pdf
- route-config-migration-plan-quant-profiles-v1.docx

Assumptions / constraints:
- Default behavior must remain unchanged when feature is off.
- Migration must be backward-compatible across control plane + routing + runtime during the train.
- Rollback must be possible via (a) per-route disable, and (b) global kill-switch, without requiring a DB rollback.

Proposed release train plan

1) PREP (by end of day Tue Mar 11)
- Land + deploy: config DB migration (adds quantization_profile_ref / disabled/default state) but no reads required.
- Land + deploy: control plane reads the new field if present, otherwise behaves as baseline.
- Land + deploy: runtime understands resolved "applied_profile_id" but treats missing as baseline.
- Land + deploy: global kill-switch config flag (default OFF / no-op).

2) STAGING VALIDATION (Wed Mar 12)
- Run integration tests (E2E) across:
  - baseline route
  - quant profile enabled route
  - incompatible profile -> fallback to baseline path
- Verify audit log event emission on enable/disable (Console/backend)
- Verify metrics:
  - quant_profile.applied_rate
  - quant_profile.fallback_rate
  - quant_profile.disabled_rate
  - p95 decode latency delta panels

3) PROD CANARY (Thu Mar 13–Mon Mar 17)
- Canary is *explicitly scoped*: allowlisted routes only.
- Proposed steps:
  - Day 1: 1% traffic on 1 design-partner route (pre-selected)
  - Day 2: 5% traffic same route if no guardrail violations
  - Day 3: 10% traffic + second route (same model variant)
  - Stop before expanding beyond allowlist until we have 48h stable signals.

Guardrails / rollback criteria (hard stop)
- Any sustained increase in 5xx (>0.2% absolute) attributed to quant-profile code path
- quant_profile.fallback_rate > 2% on canary routes for >15 mins (suggests compatibility mismatch / config drift)
- p95 latency regression > 8% on canary routes for >30 mins (after warmup)
- Quality regression alert from eval harness gating (if we run online sampling) OR customer escalation

Rollback actions (in order):
1) Disable profile on impacted route(s) (route setting to "default")
2) If still elevated, flip global kill-switch -> forces baseline precision globally
3) If still elevated, roll back runtime build (last resort; not expected)

Asks
- Dylan: confirm Console toggle will be gated behind allowlist + RBAC and that change history is visible.
- Alex: confirm docs readiness timing (we can keep docs in "beta" mode but need support-safe wording before any customer is told to use it).
- Ava: sign-off on the rollback criteria and canary timeline so Release/SRE can staff.

Thanks,
Connor O’Brien
Release Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference


---

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Mar 6, 2025 at 10:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Release train coordination: quant profile route-config migration + canary plan (Mar 11–Mar 20)

This looks good.

Console side confirmations:
- Toggle is behind feature flag + allowlist. Non-allowlisted tenants won’t see it at all.
- RBAC: only “Admin” + “Platform Operator” roles can change quant settings (aligned w/ the existing route settings permissions).
- Confirmation modal will explicitly call out: “may change outputs; evaluate before broad rollout; one-click rollback”.
- Change history: we’ll surface an entry for (a) enable/disable, and (b) profile ref change, with actor + timestamp.

Only concern: we should be crisp about "kill-switch" precedence in UI. If kill-switch is ON, Console should show "disabled by org policy" (read-only state), not look like it’s still enabled.

If you’re okay with that behavior, I’ll make sure we include it in the checklist as a validation step.

Dylan


---

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Mar 6, 2025 at 11:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: Release train coordination: quant profile route-config migration + canary plan (Mar 11–Mar 20)

Docs status:
- We can be ready with “Beta / opt-in” docs by Mar 12.
- I agree we should not publish anything customer-facing that implies “recommended/latest” auto-updates. Wording will emphasize pinning a specific profile version and explicit enablement per route.
- We’ll include a short “How to verify it’s applied” section (request log annotation / trace tag) so support has an easy play.

Request: can you add to the checklist the exact metric/log key names we want customers to look at from the Console view? Even if the full dashboards are internal, customers will ask “how do I know it worked.”

Alex Martinez
Developer Experience
Redwood Inference


---

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Mar 6, 2025 at 1:07 PM PST
Subject: Re: Release train coordination: quant profile route-config migration + canary plan (Mar 11–Mar 20)

Approved on the timeline and the general shape.

Two things I want tightened before we run a production canary:
1) Kill-switch semantics: I want it to be deterministic and fast. Please confirm expected propagation time and that it hard-forces baseline even if a route setting still points at a profile.
2) Rollback criteria: add a “customer-visible output change” clause. If a design partner reports a meaningful output change that they consider a regression, we disable immediately (don’t debate it on email).

Otherwise, proceed.

Ava


---

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Mar 6, 2025 at 2:37 PM PST
Subject: Re: Release train coordination: quant profile route-config migration + canary plan (Mar 11–Mar 20)

Ack.

Kill-switch semantics (what we will validate in staging):
- Precedence: kill-switch overrides route-level enablement. When ON, routing resolves to “baseline/default” and runtime will not attempt to load/apply a quant artifact.
- Propagation target: < 2 minutes to take effect globally (config plane propagation + cache TTL). We’ll test by flipping it in staging and watching applied_rate go to ~0 and disabled_rate go to ~1.
- Console behavior: agrees with Dylan’s note — show read-only “disabled by org policy” when kill-switch is active.

Rollback criteria update:
- Adding explicit clause to checklist: “Any design partner reports customer-visible output regression deemed unacceptable -> immediate disable on that route (no debate), then run offline evals after the fact.”

Alex: I’ll add a section with key names we can expose consistently:
- quant_profile_id (request logs / trace attribute)
- quant_profile_resolution = applied|fallback|disabled
- quant_profile_fallback_reason (if present)

I’ll upload checklist v0.4 to the same Drive folder and reply-all with the updated attachment.

Connor
